title: What things are called
intro: Memory methods have many names. Here are the common ones, in plain words, with where Mnemos teaches each. If you have heard a name before, this page tells you where to find it.

items.name: Image method
items.means: Turning an item into one vivid picture, with sound, touch and motion as well as sight.

items.name: Link method (story chain)
items.means: Joining each picture to the next in one running story, so one item leads to the next.

items.name: Palace (method of loci)
items.means: Putting each picture at a fixed place in a building you know, and walking the places in order.

items.name: Roman Room
items.means: A palace of just one room. Walls and furniture in a fixed order give you 8 to 12 stops.

items.name: Journey method
items.means: A palace made of a walk or a commute, with landmarks as the stops.

items.name: Major System
items.means: A sound code that turns digits into consonant sounds, so a number becomes a word you can picture.

items.name: Your own image list
items.means: Your personal picture for each number from 00 to 99, which you choose and keep.

items.name: Number-shape pegs
items.means: A fixed picture for each digit, based on what the digit looks like, such as a 2 that looks like a swan.

items.name: Rhyme pegs
items.means: A fixed picture for each number, based on a word that rhymes with it, such as 'one is a bun'.

items.name: Sound-alike (keyword) method
items.means: Linking a new word to a picture of a word you already know that sounds like it. Fast to start, but fades without checks.

items.name: Chunking
items.means: Cutting a long string into groups of 2 to 4, or a talk into 5 to 9 points, so each group is easier to hold.

items.name: Mind Map
items.means: A topic drawn as a middle, branches and leaves, then rebuilt from memory.

items.name: Memory rhythm
items.means: Saying groups aloud in a steady beat, as one more cue.

items.name: Skimming (Skim, Pick, Keep)
items.means: A reading step: look quickly for the key points, pick them, then keep them with pictures and places. It finds points, it does not store them.

items.name: Check Before You Look
items.means: Trying to recall from memory first, then looking, and repeating after a gap.

honest: These are tools, not a cure. They help with lists, names, orders and exact wording, when you choose to use them. Try each one and keep the ones that work for you. Your own scores on Mnemos tasks will tell you.
